primitives.name: Involuntary-to-Voluntary Ideation
primitives.verbatim_quote: A supply of ideas of the various movements that are possible left in the memory by experiences of their involuntary performance is thus the first prerequisite of the voluntary life.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I': 'dimensionless scalar representing involuntary movement memory', 'V': 'dimensionless scalar representing voluntary action readiness'}
primitives.assumptions: Memory stores invariant movement templates; voluntary control emerges from stored ideation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When I → 0, V becomes undefined due to lack of reference.

layer2.mapping: Ideational memory (I) maps to Bayesian prior distribution over motor actions (V), enabling probabilistic volition.
layer2.telemetry: Neural activation patterns during imagined vs. actual movement execution.

primitives.name: Remote Effect Distinction
primitives.verbatim_quote: All these remote effects of the movement, as we may call them, are also produced by movements which we ourselves perform ; and they leave innumerable ideas in our mind by which we distinguish each movement from the rest.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R': 'dimensionless scalar denoting remote sensory effect intensity', 'D': 'dimensionless scalar indicating discriminative capacity between movements'}
primitives.assumptions: Each movement generates unique remote sensory signatures; D increases with R.

layer2.mapping: Remote sensory data (R) forms kernel for distinguishing movement classes (D) in GSE state space.
layer2.telemetry: Auditory/visual signature correlation in motor imagery tasks.

primitives.name: Resident Impression Consciousness
primitives.verbatim_quote: But in addition to these impressions upon remote organs of sense, we have, whenever we perform a movement ourselves, another set of impressions, those, namely, which come up from the parts that are actually moved.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P': 'dimensionless scalar representing proprioceptive feedback strength', 'C': 'dimensionless scalar quantifying conscious awareness of motion'}
primitives.assumptions: Proprioception enhances self-awareness of movement; C ∝ P.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When P → 0, C becomes unreliable or absent.

layer2.mapping: Proprioceptive input (P) maps to consciousness metric (C) in GSI cognitive model.
layer2.telemetry: Electromyographic activity correlated with reported movement awareness.

reasoning_traces.think:
The foundational structure of voluntary movement cognition rests on the encoding of involuntary motor experiences into memory-based ideation. This ideation serves as a generative template for intentional action. The process involves multiple modalities: visual (sight of movement), auditory (sound of movement), and somatic (proprioceptive feedback). These modalities create a rich sensory manifold that allows for discrimination between movement types. The remote effects—visual, auditory, tactile—provide external markers that help distinguish one movement from another. Meanwhile, resident impressions from muscle and joint sensors offer internal confirmation, grounding the idea of movement in physical reality. In GSI, this translates to a hierarchical Bayesian model where prior movement hypotheses are updated with sensory evidence. In GSE, it manifests as a state transition system where movement states evolve based on multimodal sensory inputs. The failure mode occurs when any modality is disrupted—e.g., loss of proprioception leads to impaired volition, or absence of remote sensory cues reduces discriminability.
